text:
sam_sales: Hey team — on a POC with Acme Corp. They're hitting intermittent 413s when sending long chat+history payloads to our hosted endpoint through their on-prem nginx gateway. Customer says it works for shorter chats. Need quick triage and a pricing estimate for long-context runs :pray:
jenna_cust: Error snippet from their client:
```
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: inference.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 0

{...big json...}  <-- client says this is ~1.2MB / ~200k tokens before encoding
```
jenna_cust: They see an nginx 413 from the gateway, not a 4xx from our API. Logs: "upstream sent too big header" sometimes, other times: "client intended to send too large body"
deploy-bot: Deploy 2023-11-22T09:04:03Z to prod-gateway completed :white_check_mark:
lee_se: Two quick things to check on their side: client_max_body_size in nginx and any reverse-proxy / LB that enforces max request bytes. Also check if the client is unintentionally sending Content-Length: 0 + chunked body — some proxies dislike that.
anya_eng: Also worth checking whether the client uses gzip/deflate. We sometimes see middleboxes reject compressed JSON or rewrite headers and drop Content-Length which results in 413. Ask them to replay raw tcp to reproduce.
sam_sales: Can we confirm whether our hosted front-door (edge CDN / api-gateway) imposes limits? Customer is nervous about moving to Dedicated without understanding limits.
anya_eng: Our public API gateway allows up to 6MB body by default for hosted. Dedicated/private can be configured higher. However nginx/proxies in front of customers often default to much smaller limits (1MB). So likely their gateway is rejecting before hitting us.
lee_se: Suggested repro steps for them (short, copy-paste):
```
# check nginx max body
nginx -V 2>&1 | grep -i client_max_body_size || echo 'check nginx conf for client_max_body_size'
# quick curl to simulate big payload
curl -i -X POST https://inference.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  --data-binary @big_payload.json
```
jenna_cust: They tried curl and still got 413. I asked them to curl directly to our endpoint bypassing their gateway and they said it worked. So it's definitely their gateway.
sam_sales: Good find. Can SE/Eng provide a short note we can send to their infra team explaining config changes + temporary workarounds? Also customer asked: if we move to Dedicated, will token counts/costs change for long-context calls? They want an estimate for 200k-token contexts processing ~50 requests/day.
lee_se: Draft note for infra team (copyable):
"It looks like your nginx is rejecting large POST bodies. Please check/set client_max_body_size in your nginx.conf (e.g., client_max_body_size 10M;). If you're proxying to a load balancer, also check its request-size limits. If you use chunked transfer-encoding, ensure your proxy/LB supports it and doesn't require a Content-Length header. If you still see errors, enable proxy_buffering off and increase proxy_buffers/proxy_busy_buffers_size."
anya_eng: Pricing estimate for 200k-token contexts (very rough):
- If each request truly expands to 200k model tokens, tokens billed ~ input+output. For 50 req/day = 10k requests/month. That's 200k * 50 * 30 ~= 300M input tokens/month. Output depends on generation length — assume 2k tokens => +30M output. Total ~330M tokens/month. Multiply by per-token price (we can supply tiered estimate).
lee_se: Practical note: sending whole 200k dialog each time is expensive and brittle. Recommend RAG-style chunking: store embeddings of long history, retrieve top-k relevant chunks for each request (reduces to ~4-8k tokens typically). That also avoids gateway limits because you send much smaller payloads.
jenna_cust: Security note: they cannot use presigned S3 links due to corporate policy for this POC, so streaming or RAG is preferable.
sam_sales: Action items: 1) I'll forward the nginx note to the customer infra. 2) Anya/Lee — can you paste a one-paragraph explainer (config + short-term workaround) I can send to their security team? 3) I'll prepare a rough cost calc with our per-token tiers.
anya_eng: One-paragraph explainer (paste-ready):
"Your nginx/gateway is dropping large POSTs. Please increase client_max_body_size (example: 10M or larger) and confirm proxies/LBs in front of nginx don't enforce a lower max. If changing that is restricted, use a pattern where the client uploads long context to an internal store (S3 or similar) and the request to our API contains only a reference + a small retrieval window; or use streaming/chunked requests that the gateway supports. For immediate POC, reduce sent history by summarizing or retrieving relevant chunks client-side to stay well under gateway limits."
lee_se: I'll also include a short troubleshooting checklist to the thread with logs to capture if they re-open the issue (Content-Length mismatch, chunked vs non-chunked, gzipped body, LB error codes).
jenna_cust: Customer replied: infra team confirmed they had default 1M client_max_body_size + an app LB that truncates chunked bodies. They're going to try increasing to 15M and test.
sam_sales: Perfect. If they still need to send >15M payloads, we'll propose Dedicated/private with configurable gateway or recommend the RAG approach. I also asked for a sample (anonymized) big payload to sanity-check token count before they change infra.
lee_se: One more tip: if they must send big attachments, consider uploading to a secure blobstore and sending a signed one-time URL (if policy allows). That way our API receives a small JSON with the URL and can fetch server-side, avoiding gateway limits.
jenna_cust: They're paused on presigned URLs due to security, so will try the nginx change first.
sam_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll update once infra tests. :thumbsup:
